therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Number of participants who experienced at least one adverse event

results.effect_size: No discontinuations due to AE at most doses; 1 discontinuation at 100 mg; AEs occurred in 1–3 participants per dose cohort
results.target_engagement_evidence: Dose-dependent reduction in 24-hour weighted mean glucose concentration observed across dose range 15–170 mg
biomarker_changes: 24-hour weighted mean glucose (WMG) decreased dose-dependently vs placebo: -8.1 mg/dL at 15 mg (p=0.368), -16.6 mg/dL at 30 mg (p=0.079), -25.7 mg/dL at 45 mg (p=0.007), -36.3 mg/dL at 60 mg (p<0.001), -57.6 mg/dL at 80 mg (p<0.001), -28.9 mg/dL at 100 mg (p=0.026), -43.9 mg/dL at 140 mg (p<0.001), -59.4 mg/dL at 170 mg (p<0.001)
AUC(0-∞) increased with dose from 489 nM*hr at 15 mg to 9560 nM*hr at 170 mg
Cmax increased with dose from 37.3 nM at 15 mg to 912 nM at 170 mg
Apparent terminal half-life ranged from 17.0 to 22.1 hours across doses
Fed state (60 mg fed) reduced AUC(0-∞) by ~8% (geometric mean ratio 0.92) and Cmax by ~19% (geometric mean ratio 0.81) vs fasted
safety_signals: 1 participant discontinued treatment due to an AE at the 100 mg dose
3 participants experienced at least one AE at the 80 mg dose, the highest incidence across cohorts
No discontinuations due to AEs at doses 15–80 mg or 140–170 mg
1 participant each experienced at least one AE at 15 mg, 30 mg, 60 mg, 60 mg fed, 100 mg, 140 mg, 170 mg, placebo, and placebo fed

dose_info.dose: 15 mg, 30 mg, 45 mg, 60 mg, 80 mg, 100 mg, 140 mg, 170 mg (single oral doses)

context.duration: Up to approximately 31 days (run-in through poststudy period)
